MODALITY, taken from the source text's verbs.
domain-seizure -- "Nell'operazione sono stati sequestrati oltre 200 Server e 80 domini e sono state effettuate 20 perquisizioni in tutta Europa presso sedi di società e provider." (polizia raw:20) and "oltre al sequestro ed all'oscuramento della intera piattaforma Xtream Codes, di 80 siti internet e di 183 server dedicati alla riproduzione e diffusione dei flussi audiovisivi" (gdf raw:23). Judicial seizure of 80 domains/sites: state process, control transferred.
hosting-takedown -- the same two lines carry the servers (200+ / 183), and polizia raw:20 states the result: "rendere inattiva la complessa infrastruttura tecnologica operante a livello internazionale".
arrest-search -- "Oltre 100 militari del Nucleo Speciale Tutela Privacy e Frodi Tecnologiche e dei reparti territoriali della Guardia di Finanza stanno eseguendo, in queste ore, provvedimenti di perquisizione locale, informatica e conseguente sequestro" (gdf raw:15); "25 gli obiettivi delle perquisizioni odierne sul territorio nazionale" (gdf raw:25); the eight EIOs executed abroad "nei confronti di 3 aziende e 5 persone fisiche" (gdf raw:23); and the 20 European searches at company and provider premises (polizia raw:20). NOT payment-disruption, and this is the closest call on the row. The census rationale for this component says PayPal accounts were blocked, but no publisher text in any usable capture uses the verb blocked or gives the figure 150. The only usable account of that measure is the GdF's, which frames it as sequestro of 197 rapporti finanziari aimed at the proceeds -- asset-seizure, already coded. NOT end-user-action -- gdf raw:25 closes with "nei confronti dei fruitori del servizio è prevista la reclusione da sei mesi a 3 anni e la multa fino a 25.822 Euro": the statutory penalty range applicable to subscribers, i.e. what the law allows, not a measure applied to any identified end user in this action.
NOT blocking-order -- oscuramento appears only in the same breath as sequestro of the platform, the sites and the servers (gdf raw:23): control taken, not access blocked with the site left standing. No DNS/ISP order or dynamic injunction is described.
NOT intermediary-process -- the eight EIOs were executed as searches and seizures against companies and natural persons (gdf raw:23), which arrest-search carries; no disclosure request to a registrar, host or CDN is described.
NOT content-delisting -- no notice-and-takedown, delisting or platform-side removal in either 2019 release; the 350 Telegram channels belong to the 2020 component.

JUDICIAL.
arrests not-reported -- neither release states an arrest, and neither describes the outcome completely enough for the absence to be a fact: the GdF release is written while the searches are still running, "stanno eseguendo, in queste ore" (gdf raw:15). RECONSTITUTION relaunch-reported, as_of 2020-11-11. The evidence postdates the coded action by fourteen months and comes from a usable capture. Eurojust's November 2020 release states what the 2019 action did -- "In a major operation in September 2019 led by the Italian desk at Eurojust, over 200 servers were taken down to prevent the fraud from propagating." (raw/press-releases/2020-11-11_eurojust_new-major-crackdown-on-fraud-with-illegal-use-of-pay-tv-signals.md:45) -- and then that "Investigations into this particular network have been ongoing for some time, leading to the further action taken this week." Eurojust's National Member for Italy frames it the same way: "After the major operation in Italy of last year, we haven’t stopped to assist and support our national authorities. (polizia raw:18), independently corroborated by the GdF, whose eight EIOs "sono stati eseguiti simultaneamente questa mattina in Olanda, Francia, Grecia, Germania e Bulgaria dalle rispettive polizie giudiziarie" (gdf raw:23). Coding open-question from a generic 'reconstitution is not precluded' observation would make the value non-discriminating across the corpus. This is a rule-interpretation call, not a reading of the record, and the coordinator can flip it consistently across the census if the literal reading is preferred; the same reasoning is recorded on portugal-spain-europol-euipo-… where I rejected open-question for a related reason. CAPTURE TIER: USABLE. raw/press-releases/2025-02-17_policia-es_… (curl_cffi, http 200, 865 words) carries the verbatim Spanish release — headline and standfirsts at raw:111-121, body at raw:123-135 — inside heavy policia.es site chrome (raw:33-109, raw:139-221). One handling note: raw:25, ABOVE the '## Extracted Summary' heading, is an agent-written Spanish digest of the release, not release text; it is reconstruction and is not cited (it also drifts from the original — it writes 'granja de minería de criptomonedas' where the release says 'granja de minado', and 'equipo de minería de alto rendimiento' where the release says 'equipos informáticos de alto rendimiento'). MODALITY: blocking-order — the release's verb is bloquear throughout, from the headline 'La Policía Nacional bloquea seis páginas web dedicadas a la difusión ilícita de videojuegos y contenido audiovisual IPTV' (raw:113) to the lede 'Agentes de la Policía Nacional han bloqueado seis páginas web dedicadas a la difusión ilícita de videojuegos y contenido audiovisual IPTV.' (raw:123). NOT domain-seizure: no seizure, transfer, redirect or banner is stated for the six sites, and the operation page reaches the same conclusion explicitly ('recorded here because the action was a blocking measure, not a domain seizure; domains_seized stays 0 structurally') — a correctly-resisted frontmatter seed, unlike several other rows in this census. The release does not say what instrument the blocking ran on (no court order, no ISP, no registrar is named); it is coded on the verb. arrest-search — 'Han sido detenidas tres personas en Cartagena (Murcia), Coria del Río (Sevilla) y Móstoles (Madrid)' (raw:123) and the house search, 'se realizó una entrada y registro en el domicilio del líder de la organización' (raw:135). asset-seizure — 'donde se han intervenido 72.000 euros, criptoactivos, un vehículo de alta gama y multitud de equipos informáticos de alto rendimiento.' (raw:135, standfirst version at raw:117). This is proceeds seizure, not evidence collection: the release's own frame is that the network diverted and laundered its profits ('usurpaban identidades mediante documentación falsa para desviar los beneficios que obtenían y que blanqueaban a través de una “granja de minado” de criptomonedas', raw:123), so the cash, the cryptoassets and the high-end vehicle are laundered proceeds. The high-performance computing equipment is instrumentality/evidence and is not what carries the code. NOT coded: hosting-takedown — no server or hosting infrastructure is stated seized or shut down; the mining rigs at the leader's home are the LAUNDERING vehicle, not the streaming infrastructure, and reading them as a server seizure would be a category error (the operation page keeps servers_seized 0, correctly). payment-disruption — the mining farm was seized as an asset, but no processor or advertising cutoff is described. end-user-action — more than 16,000 paying users are quantified ('seis páginas web, dirigidas dese la ciudad murciana de Cartagena, que proporcionaban suscripciones de IPTV (películas, series y fútbol) así como videojuegos a más de 16.000 usuarios que abonaban diferentes tarifas por el servicio ilícito.', raw:127 — the typo 'dese' for 'desde' is the original's) but NO action against any of them is stated; the users are a scale measure only. content-delisting, intermediary-process, voluntary-transfer — no supporting verb. JUDICIAL: arrests n=3 (raw:123, restated at raw:135, 'se llevó a cabo su arresto en las ciudades de Cartagena, Coria del Río y Móstoles'); the three roles are enumerated as leader (Cartagena), socio (Coria del Río) and ayudante (Móstoles) at raw:129, so the count is also derivable from enumeration. indictments not-reported, and this was the row's one real judgement call. The release repeatedly calls the leader 'el principal investigado' (raw:117, 123, 135), which in Spanish procedure since 2015 is the formal status of a person subject to a judicial investigation, and the house search implies a judicial warrant — so a proceeding demonstrably exists. I still coded not-reported rather than pending because v2 requires the RECORD to state that proceedings are underway, referred or awaited, and this release states none of that: it reports a completed police action and stops. This is deliberately a narrower call than the one I made on germany-zcb-kripo-weiden-…, where the prosecuting authority wrote in terms that the investigations continue; here there is no such sentence. The operation page agrees ('indictments/convictions are structural zeros, not verified outcomes'; 'reports no indictment stage; whether prosecutions followed is unknown from this source'). convictions and imprisonments not-reported — no cited record reaches either stage; detention on arrest is not an imposed custodial sentence. latest_record_date 2025-02-17 = the release date, the only record. The row is right-censored at the arrest/blocking stage roughly 18 months before coding, with no follow-on record anywhere in the corpus. RECONSTITUTION: not-reported. The release says nothing about the six sites after the blocking — no down-status check, no relaunch, no successor, and the sites are not even named, which forecloses any later verification from this record. No other record about this action exists. CONTEXT (not coded): the case's distinguishing feature is the laundering layer — 'Esta actividad les permitía ingresar adicionalmente 6.000 euros mensuales y, al mismo tiempo, blanquear de esta forma los beneficios obtenidos ilícitamente con las plataformas web.' (raw:133), on top of more than EUR 1,100,000 in subscription profit (raw:129). Referral structure: 'La investigación se inició en 2022 tras recibirse sendas denuncias de dos entidades del sector audiovisual y de entretenimiento' — Mediaproducción SLU (LaLiga) and ACE, one complaint each, not a joint filing (raw:125); both referrers are private, so this is a single-sovereign rights-holder-referral action, as the operation page's missing_fields already records. CORPUS SEARCH (grep -rlie 'cartagena|coria del r|granja de minado|16.000 usuarios' over wiki/sources/): the only hit is the single cited source page. NO linkage gap, and no second record exists for this action anywhere in the corpus. CORPUS DEFECTS FOUND (minor, reported not fixed): (1) NEW — the operation page's Results and Impact says 'high-performance mining equipment seized', but the release's seizure list says 'multitud de equipos informáticos de alto rendimiento' (high-performance COMPUTER equipment, raw:135); the mining farm is described separately (raw:133) and the release never identifies the seized machines as the mining rigs. The results.other bullet hedges this correctly ('computer/mining rigs') while the prose does not. (2) NEW — the raw capture's own preamble line (raw:25) paraphrases the release with two altered terms ('granja de minería de criptomonedas' for 'granja de minado'; 'equipo de minería' for 'equipos informáticos'), which is likely where the prose drift entered; the preamble sits inside an otherwise verbatim capture and could be mistaken for release text. (3) MINOR — frontmatter enforcement_type lists 'takedown' where the record's only site-level verb is blocking; the page's own results.other note flags the distinction, so the structured field is the outlier.

CORPUS-SEARCH FIND (input rule 3) — THE OPERATION PAGE IS MISSING ITS BEST SOURCE. The page's frontmatter `sources` lists only two entries (the PJ Portugal capture and a 2024 EUIPO/Europol strategic report), and its References section names the Europol newsroom release by URL only. But the corpus HOLDS that release as a full source page and a usable capture: wiki/sources/2025-11-19_europol_eur-47-million-crypto-traced-disrupt-digital-piracy.md → raw/press-releases/2025-11-19_europol_eur-47-million-crypto-traced-disrupt-digital-piracy.md (jina, 674 words, http 200, full release body at raw:27-63). Its source page even lists this operation in pages_updated. Found with `ls wiki/sources/ | grep '^2025-11'` plus a content grep for '11.8 million|69 piracy|cyber-patrol week|crypto traced'. Coded as an input per rule 3; the linkage gap is reported for the coordinator to repair on the wiki side. It matters: without it this whole row would have been page-only. CAPTURE TIERS: (a) EUROPOL (corpus-search) is USABLE — verbatim own-domain release body raw:27-63 inside a small newsletter/metadata tail (raw:65-105). (b) PJ PORTUGAL (raw/press-releases/2025-11-19_pj-portugal_…) is RECONSTRUCTION tier: it is an agent-compiled dossier headed 'Source extract (verbatim and translated key passages)' (raw:24) with sections it wrote itself — a cross-source corroboration table (raw:69-81), an 'L24 cooperating-LE roster' (raw:83-91), an 'L25 tier-1 publisher justification' (raw:93-97) and 'Scope limits' (raw:99-102). It does carry genuine Portuguese verbatim fragments from the PJ release (raw:33, 36, 40), but its Europol section (B) is explicitly assembled at second hand — 'page is a Single-Page Application; full body confirmed via Infosecurity Magazine, OCCRP, Cybernews, EuroWeeklyNews, Piracy Monitor mirror reporting that reproduced Europol-supplied figures.' (raw:52) — which is the manual's WebSearch-summary tell. Cited only with the (reconstruction) marker. (c) The 2024-10-23 EUIPO/Europol 'Uncovering the ecosystem of IP crime' report predates this action by 13 months and is generic strategic analysis, not a record of this week; nothing coded from it. MODALITY: payment-disruption ONLY, and it is raw-level thanks to the Europol capture — '25 illicit IPTV services referred to the participating crypto service providers for disruption;' (europol raw:43) and, decisively for whether the disruption HAPPENED rather than was merely requested, 'By identifying, tracing, and successfully shutting down the crypto accounts of illicit services, the criminal revenue stream is disrupted.' (europol raw:53). The PJ dossier records the same outcome in its summary line on dismantled clandestine financial circuits and interrupted criminal funding flows (pj raw:46). NOT coded, and each omission is a deliberate call: asset-seizure — the EUR 47m/USD 55m is TRACED, not seized: 'Investigators traced cryptocurrency valued at around USD 55 million (over EUR 47 million) through various accounts associated with these services.' (europol raw:47); no freeze, forfeiture or judicial seizure appears in either record, and the operation page says so itself ('The figure traced is a tracing volume, not a court-ordered seizure or confiscation total'). This contradicts the page's own frontmatter seeds — enforcement_type includes `asset_freeze` and mechanisms_used includes `[[cryptocurrency-seizure]]` — which is exactly the frontmatter-seed caveat v2 warns about; the code follows the source verbs. intermediary-process — the operators were identified by OSINT and by investigators buying the services themselves (europol raw:51), not by compelled disclosure to a registrar/CDN/host; the exchange referrals are the disruption itself, already counted as payment-disruption. arrest-search, domain-seizure, hosting-takedown, blocking-order, content-delisting, end-user-action — none stated; '69 sites identified and targeted' (europol raw:41) is identification, and 'Investigations on 44 additional sites' (europol raw:45) is investigative opening. This row is one of the census's rare single-modality, no-judicial rows, and that is the substantive finding about it: a five-day co-located OSINT-and-payment-rails sprint whose only executed enforcement output is crypto-account closure by private exchanges. JUDICIAL: all four stages not-reported, empty cites. No cited record names a suspect, an arrest, a charge or a court. Europol's forward-looking line is about SERVICES, not persons — 'Several of the services remain under continued investigation by both public and private entities.' (europol raw:47) — and the PJ dossier's own scope note says 'No arrests are claimed in the tier-1 sources for this specific cyber-patrol week.' (pj raw:102). I considered `pending` for indictments on the strength of the 44 opened probes and rejected it: v2's pending needs proceedings underway against someone, and both records are explicit that no criminal organisation, operator identity or nationality was disclosed. latest_record_date 2025-11-19 = both same-day releases; the row is right-censored at announcement, with no follow-on record in the corpus. RECONSTITUTION: not-reported. I considered `open-question` because the operation page flags unresolved gaps ('closure status by named exchange not disclosed in tier-1 sources', Follow-Up Actions; the 'Disruption-vs-prosecution gap', Challenges) and rejected it: those gaps are about whether the disruption OUTPUT was executed and prosecuted, not about whether the targets reconstituted. Column 3 asks what happened to the targets after the action, and on that question every cited record is silent — no down-status, no relaunch, no successor, and the targeted services are not even named. Coding open-question here would fold 'we cannot verify the enforcement output' into a variable that measures target durability, which would pollute it; `not-reported` is the honest value. CONFLICTS/CORRECTIONS: (1) The operation page's Contradictions callout asserts a 'Currency discrepancy: PJ release says USD 55 million; Europol release says EUR 47 million.' That is wrong on the Europol side — the Europol release itself gives BOTH figures in one sentence, 'around USD 55 million (over EUR 47 million)' (europol raw:47) — so there is no inter-release discrepancy to reconcile. The uncited Europol capture settles a question the page left open. (2) Visitor figure: Europol's precise number is 11 821 006 (europol raw:47); the page's '~11.8 million' is a faithful rounding. (3) Attribution: the Europol release names only Europol, EUIPO and the Spanish National Police (europol raw:37) — Portugal and the Polícia Judiciária/UNC3T appear only in the PJ release (pj raw:33), and the seven private-sector partners (AAPA, Binance, Chainalysis, Coinbase, Irdeto, Maltego, Premier League) are named only in the PJ dossier (pj raw:44, 67), not in the Europol text. The page presents the partner list without that attribution split. (4) 'More than 15 countries and private sector organisations joined Europol in this collaborative effort' (europol raw:59) — the page's restriction of participating_countries to Portugal and Spain is correct and well-founded. CORPUS SEARCH: `ls wiki/sources/ | grep '^2025-11'` (89 files) plus `grep -rlie '11.8 million|69 piracy|cyber-patrol week|crypto traced|cryptocurrency traced' wiki/sources/` returned nine hits; only two are about this action — the cited PJ page and the UNCITED Europol page above. No source page exists in the corpus for any of the four tier-2 outlets the operation page lists in its References (Infosecurity Magazine, OCCRP, Cybernews, Piracy Monitor), so those references are unbacked by any capture. CORPUS DEFECTS FOUND (reported, not fixed): (1) NEW and material — the missing `sources` entry for the Europol own-domain release described above; the page cites it as a bare URL in References while the corpus holds both a source page and a usable full-text capture, and the source page's own Cross-references section already points back at this operation. (2) NEW — the 'Currency discrepancy' open question in Contradictions & Open Questions is resolved by that same capture and should be closed. (3) NEW — the frontmatter's `enforcement_type: asset_freeze` and `mechanisms_used: [[cryptocurrency-seizure]]` are not supported by either record (traced ≠ frozen ≠ seized); the page's own prose says so, so the structured fields and the prose disagree. (4) NEW — the References section lists four tier-2 outlets with no corresponding source pages or captures in the corpus, i.e. they are uncheckable citations.

MODALITY: arrest-search — 'Oltre cento operatori della Polizia postale hanno effettuato perquisizioni nei confronti di 31 indagati in 11 città del nostro Paese e 14 obiettivi situati all’estero, in collaborazione con le Forze di polizia di Regno Unito, Spagna, Romania, Kosovo.' (polizia raw:129), corroborated by ACE's '29 raids in 11 Italian cities' (ace raw:78) and by DOJ for the Romanian leg, 'ICHIP-mentored Romanian economic police officers conducted searches and issued a subpoena for interrogation in three Romanian cities' (doj raw:223). hosting-takedown — 'In Italia sono state sequestrate tre piattaforme Iptv illegali' (polizia raw:141), 'Illegal IPTV infrastructure serving millions of users taken offline' (ace raw:84), 'Six servers seized outside of Italy' (ace raw:94). domain-seizure — the same Italian sentence states judicial seizure banners were affixed to the front-end sites: 'con apposizione di pannelli di sequestro ai siti vetrina e gruppi Telegram utilizzati per la vendita' (polizia raw:141); a seizure panel served under a Catania prosecutorial order is transfer of site control under state process, which is exactly the v2 redirect-as-control case. content-delisting — the Telegram sales channels in that same clause, plus ACE's 'Removal of associated websites and Telegram-based sales channels' (ace raw:92): messaging-channel and associated-site removal is the v2 content-delisting scope. end-user-action is a BORDERLINE CALL, coded the same way as the Kenya row so the census stays internally consistent: 'L'operazione ha bloccato l'attività di un migliaio di rivenditori italiani con oscuramento di oltre 100mila utenti finali in Italia e milioni a livello mondiale.' (polizia raw:139) and 'More than 125,000 end users disconnected in Italy, and millions globally' (ace raw:88). Reading A (coded): the records report end users as a direct object of the action and both sides publish the count as a headline result. Reading B (rejected, recorded): disconnection is the downstream effect of shutting the service, and no end user faces any stated proceeding — under that reading end-user-action should be reserved for enforcement against users (the Italian/Greek fine tracks). Flagging so the coordinator can normalise this code across the census; it is the same judgement call as multichoice-irdeto-kenya-… NOT coded: asset-seizure — the release describes financial-flow ANALYSIS, not seizure ('tracciamento delle transazioni finanziarie, soprattutto in criptovalute', polizia raw:133) and describes the suspects' own crypto investment, fictitious asset registration and shell companies as offence conduct (raw:135); no freeze, forfeiture or confiscation is stated and the operation page's cryptocurrency_seized is empty. blocking-order, payment-disruption, intermediary-process, voluntary-transfer — no supporting verb. JUDICIAL: arrests not-reported. No cited record states a single arrest: the Italian release reports searches against 31 indagati (raw:129), ACE reports '31 suspects' identified (ace raw:78), and DOJ reports only that 'An international arrest warrant was issued for a Romanian target' (doj raw:223) — a warrant issued is not an arrest executed (same call as the Operação 404 fase-8 row on its four preventive-arrest warrants). (polizia raw:125), those 31 are formally indagati under search (raw:129), and an international arrest warrant has issued for one target (doj raw:223) — proceedings underway, but indizi di colpevolezza and indagato status are pre-trial investigative categories in Italian procedure, not rinvio a giudizio, so this is not n=31. The wiki source page uses 2026-04-18 and so do I. (The operation page's References table lists this same DOJ source twice with the two different dates, rows [3] 2026-04-18 and [6] 2022-02-22 — see corpus defects.) RECONSTITUTION: not-reported. No cited record speaks to what happened after. ACE's 'infrastructure … taken offline' (ace raw:84) is announcement-day status published 2026-01-29, within days of the 22-28 January action and far inside the 14-day window, so it is not durability evidence. The DOJ record, whose content postdates the action by roughly two months, recounts the action without any status statement about the platforms or the six servers. No successor is named and no relaunch is reported. CONFLICTS ACROSS RECORDS (none of these is a coded Column value; all recorded per the manual): (1) RESELLERS — the Italian tier-1 says roughly a thousand, 'un migliaio di rivenditori italiani' (polizia raw:139), while ACE says 'Approximately 250 Italian resellers dismantled' (ace raw:86); the operation page adopts ACE's 250. A four-fold divergence between the official release and the rights-holder coalition, unexplained in both. (2) END USERS — 'oltre 100mila utenti finali in Italia' (polizia raw:139) versus 'More than 125,000 end users disconnected in Italy' (ace raw:88); the page adopts ACE's figure. (3) 14 COUNTRIES vs 14 TARGETS — the Italian release says searches hit '11 città del nostro Paese e 14 obiettivi situati all’estero' (polizia raw:129), i.e. 14 TARGETS abroad; ACE renders this as '29 raids in 11 Italian cities and 14 countries worldwide' (ace raw:78) and the operation page repeats '14 countries worldwide' in results.other and Results and Impact — while naming only eight foreign jurisdictions anywhere. (polizia raw:143), with no seizure verb. (5) DAMAGE FIGURE — DOJ reports '$3.5 billion USD' of rightsholder damage (doj raw:223) while the Italian release quantifies only 'un giro di affari di milioni di euro mensili' (polizia raw:137); the operation page carries neither as a structured field.
